items.content: It’s a new way into the cloud. GeForce NOW welcomes Firefox support to the cloud, opening up another way to jump into high-performance PC gaming straight from the browser, starting today. Whether on a school laptop or everyday PC, it’s now even easier to play supported PC games without downloading a dedicated app. Plus, discover 12 new games streaming from the GeForce NOW library this week, led by Gallipoli. No Downloads. Just Firefox. This cloud is on fire with new ways to play on Firefox. GeForce NOW is now supported on Firefox, expanding access across even more devices. Members can outfox big downloads and jump into high-performance PC gaming directly from the browser — no waiting on lengthy game installs or updates. The experience delivers GeForce RTX-powered performance at up to 1440p and 120 frames per second for GeForce NOW Ultimate members. Simply download the latest version of Firefox, head to play.geforcenow.com and start playing. The cloud handles the heavy lifting, so games are ready to play without taking up valuable storage space on the device. Firefox joins Chrome, Edge and Opera in supporting GeForce NOW on Windows browsers. Deploy the Games Land on the beaches of the Gallipoli Peninsula in BlackMill Games’ Gallipoli, the latest entry in the WW1 Game Series. Fight as soldiers of the British and Ottoman Empires in intense 25v25 objective-based battles across coastal shores, deserts and urban battlefields, with 10 historical classes and over 50 authentic weapons and equipment options. Teamwork is key in its grounded, one-shot-one-kill combat. Take command as an Officer, provide cover as a Heavy Machine Gunner or Sniper, keep the squad going as a Stretcher Bearer and more while navigating challenging campaigns. Head to the frontlines from the cloud with no lengthy game downloads or installs taking up local storage space. Play directly in the newly supported Firefox browser, or take the action across PCs, Macs, Chromebooks, handhelds and more with GeForce NOW cloud saves. In addition, members can look for the following games streaming throughout the week: Stars Reach (New release on Steam, Aug. 18) The Sinking City 2 (New release on Steam, Aug. 18) Gallipoli (New release on Steam, Aug. 20) DIVE or DIE – Children of Rain (Steam) Escape the Backroom (Xbox, available on Game Pass) Hell Is Us (Xbox, available on Game Pass) High on Life (Steam) High on Life 2 (Steam and Xbox, available on Game Pass) Parcel Simulator (Steam) Starvester (Steam) The Thaumaturge (Xbox, available on Game Pass) Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered (Epic Games Store) Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after release and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates on announced titles. To try GeForce NOW in Firefox, start with a GeForce NOW day pass and experience premium cloud gaming directly from the browser. If members later upgrade to a Performance or Ultimate membership, the cost of the day pass can be applied toward the first membership purchase. What are you planning to play this weekend? Let us know on X or in the comments below.

items.descriptionZh:
NVIDIA 旗下的云游戏平台 GeForce NOW 今日宣布正式支持 Firefox 浏览器，为用户提供了一条进入云端高性能 PC 游戏世界的新路径。此前，GeForce NOW 已可在 Chrome、Edge 和 Opera 等 Windows 浏览器上运行，Firefox 的加入进一步扩大了其设备覆盖范围。这意味着，无论是学校配发的笔记本电脑，还是日常使用的普通 PC，玩家无需下载专用客户端或等待漫长的游戏安装与更新，只需安装最新版 Firefox，访问 play.geforcenow.com 即可直接开始游戏。

从技术原理上看，GeForce NOW 采用云端渲染与视频流传输方案：游戏在 NVIDIA 远程数据中心的高性能服务器上运行，画面经过编码压缩后实时推送到用户浏览器，而玩家的操作指令则以低延迟方式回传至云端。所有计算负载都在云端完成，因此本地设备几乎不占用存储空间，也无需强大的图形处理器，从而大幅降低了进入高品质 PC 游戏的门槛。对于 Ultimate 会员，该服务可提供由 GeForce RTX 驱动的性能输出，最高支持 1440p 分辨率和每秒 120 帧的流畅体验。同时，结合 GeForce NOW 的云存档功能，玩家可以在 PC、Mac、Chromebook、掌机等多种设备间无缝切换，随时随地继续游戏进度。

本周 GeForce NOW 还同步引入了 12 款新游戏，其中以 BlackMill Games 开发的《Gallipoli》最受瞩目。该作是“一战游戏系列”的最新成员，背景设定在加里波利半岛登陆战役。玩家将分别扮演英国与奥斯曼帝国的士兵，在海岸、沙漠和城市战场中参与 25v25 的目标导向战斗。游戏提供 10 个历史职业，如指挥官、重机枪手、狙击手、担架兵等，并收录了超过 50 种真实的武器与装备。其战斗风格强调写实与团队协作，每一发子弹都可能致命，医疗兵能否及时救人、军官能否有效指挥，往往决定战局走向。由于游戏通过云端流式传输，玩家无需在本地下载体积庞大的游戏文件，可直接在新增支持的 Firefox 浏览器中投入前线战斗。

本周其他新增游戏还包括《Stars Reach》（8 月 18 日发售）、《The Sinking City 2》（8 月 18 日发售）、《DIVE or DIE – Children of Rain》、《Escape the Backroom》（Xbox/Game Pass）、《Hell Is Us》（Xbox/Game Pass）、《High on Life》（Steam）、《High on Life 2》（Steam 和 Xbox/Game Pass）、《Parcel Simulator》（Steam）、《Starvester》（Steam）、《The Thaumaturge》（Xbox/Game Pass）以及《Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered》（Epic Games Store）。需要留意的是，上述日期对应游戏在各自商店的首发时间，GeForce NOW 的上线时间可能会因游戏入库流程而略有延迟，NVIDIA 会在每周的“GFN Thursday”中公布确切的可用信息。

为了让更多用户体验这一新入口，GeForce NOW 推出了优惠方案：用户可以直接在 Firefox 中购买单日通行证尝试云端游戏，如果后续升级为 Performance 或 Ultimate 会员，日通行证的费用还可抵扣首笔会员订阅费。这一举措既降低了尝鲜成本，也为希望在浏览器中直接体验 GeForce RTX 性能的玩家提供了灵活选择。随着浏览器端支持的不断扩展，GeForce NOW 正在将高端 PC 游戏从笨重的硬件束缚中解放出来，使超低门槛、跨设备的云端游戏体验真正走进日常生活。

items.content: Slack is introducing dedicated channels where teams can vibe-code together with AI agents instead of jumping between different tools and conversations. The Slack Code launch includes open, project-specific code channels with dedicated user tabs, alongside features that compare coding changes and preview HTML output before the project is shipped.“With Slack Code, when you have an idea or need to build a new feature, update a web page, or fix a bug, you simply tag in a coding agent like Anthropic’s Claude or Cognition’s Devin, and that agent then spins up a code channel to tackle the task,” Slack said in its press release. “There, everyone has full visibility to the conversation, can audit code diffs, get live previews of the agent’s output, give feedback, and approve the work before it ships.”The coding channels are designed to archive themselves automatically upon completion of their dedicated assignments, and provide an audit log for recordkeeping. Slack is pitching this feature as an easy way to work collaboratively with AI agents “like teammates” — a mentality that SpaceXAI is also trying to sell people on with its new Grok Bot agents.Here’s a quick simulated demonstration of how Slack Code channels work. GIF: SlackSlack Code is available starting today on any Slack plan. It’ll work with the AI agents available on Slack’s marketplace, and Slack says that agents from its founding partners — including Claude Code, Devin, Vercel Agent, and GitHub Copilot — will “integrate seamlessly” with code channels.

items.titleZh: Slack is launching collaborative vibe-coding channels
items.descriptionZh:
Slack 正式推出全新功能 Slack Code，为团队提供专门的代码协作频道，允许开发人员与 AI 代理在同一工作空间内“边聊天边写代码”，无需在不同工具和对话窗口之间来回切换。这一功能的核心理念是让 AI 代理像队友一样参与项目开发，将原本分散在 IDE、聊天工具和代码评审平台中的工作流整合进 Slack 统一界面。

在具体使用方式上，当用户产生新想法、需要开发新功能、更新网页或修复 Bug 时，只需在 Slack 中提及一个编码代理（如 Anthropic 的 Claude、Cognition 的 Devin），该代理就会自动创建一个专属代码频道来接管任务。团队所有成员都可以在这个频道中完整查看对话记录，审查代码差异（code diff），实时预览代理生成的 HTML 输出，提出反馈意见，并在项目正式上线前批准最终成果。这种设计使得整个开发过程透明可追踪，每个参与者的贡献和决策都有迹可循。

Slack Code 的频道具备自动归档功能，当特定任务完成后，代码频道会自动封存，保持工作区整洁有序。同时，系统会生成完整的审计日志，便于后续回顾合规记录或复盘开发流程。这一特性特别适合需要严格文档管理的企业环境。Slack 将这一功能定位为“与 AI 代理像队友一样协作”的便捷方式，与 SpaceXAI 正在推广的 Grok Bot 代理理念不谋而合。

该功能自发布之日起即可在所有 Slack 套餐中使用。兼容性方面，Slack Code 支持 Slack 应用市场上已有的各类 AI 代理，并且 Slack 表示，其创始合作伙伴——包括 Claude Code、Devin、Vercel Agent 和 GitHub Copilot——所推出的代理将与代码频道实现“无缝集成”。这意味着企业可以在不更换现有工具链的情况下，直接借助 Slack Code 将 AI 代理的工作成果纳入团队协作流程。

从技术影响来看，Slack Code 标志着 AI 辅助编程从“个人开发者工具”走向“团队协作基础设施”的重要转变。它解决了此前 AI 编码代理输出缺乏审查机制和协作上下文的问题——通过将所有生成内容置于团队可见的频道中，结合代码差异对比和实时预览功能，既保留了 AI 的高效生成能力，又增加了人工审核的安全阀。对于采用 AI 编程代理的团队，尤其是远程分布式团队，Slack Code 有望减少上下文切换成本，加速迭代速度，同时确保代码质量和合规性。应用场景覆盖产品功能开发、网页快速改版、Bug 修复、原型验证等各类需要快速产出代码并多人协作的环节。

items.title: The supercomputer race no longer means what it used to, as rankings lose relevance in the AI era — as privately held compute clusters are built, running HPL becomes a distraction
items.description: We review the current state of high-performance supercomputing, interviewing experts, including the deputy head of high-performance computing at GWDG, to find out exactly where the current race stands.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter China's LineShine is the world's fastest supercomputer – though having said that, it does depend on who exactly is counting. The machine, based in the National Supercomputing Center in Shenzhen, debuted at number one in the June 2026 TOP500 list published in mid-July because of its eye-popping results, with nearly 2.2 exaflops, or more than two quintillion floating-point calculations per second. The system also topped the competing HPCG ranking. But the picture was more mixed taken in the round: LineShine finished fourth on the mixed-precision HPL-MxP test and was well off the pace on the Green500 energy-efficiency table.The gap for the supercomputer sits depending on who's ranking it, showing how what used to be a simple race for supremacy has actually become several overlapping competitions. It also highlights how "fastest" has different definitions depending on what is measured, how it is measured, and which operators publish their results.We previously reported how LineShine uses 13.79 million cores built around China's domestic LingKun platform, 304-core LX2 processors, the proprietary LingQi interconnect, and Kylin operating system. It's also the first CPU-only machine on the TOP500 to sustain more than two exaflops, reaching around 80% of its theoretical peak while drawing 42.2 megawatts. That makes it impressive enough – but it’s also a big win on a geopolitical stage.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: China rising (Image credit: AMD)LineShine is the first Chinese system to lead the TOP500 since 2017, ending a period in which China stopped submitting its most advanced machines to the public ranking. Jack Dongarra, emeritus professor of computer science at the University of Tennessee and one of the TOP500's founders, has previously said that two unreported Chinese systems may already have been faster than the then-leading US machine, Frontier.The TOP500 has used the High Performance Linpack benchmark, or HPL, since the ranking began in 1993. In the test, computers have to solve a dense web system of linear equations using double-precision arithmetic. Like many tests, the regularity of it can be heavily tuned, producing a clean output that invites long-run comparisons across architectures and decades. You may like China's LineShine supercomputer dethrones El Capitan in Top 500 list China tops the list of fastest supercomputers with a CPU-only behemoth, ending US champion El Capitan's reign China's Moonshot AI reportedly used Nvidia Blackwell chips for training Kimi K3 It’s tempting to look at rankings like this as the be-all and end-all, but even TOP500 says its result doesn’t reflect a machine's overall performance, because no single number can. But HPL remains valuable because it tests whether millions of processor cores and the links between them can be corralled into one tightly coordinated calculation. "It shows you can go 400 kilometres per hour with your Porsche," said Julian Kunkel, professor of high-performance computing at the University of Göttingen and deputy head of high-performance computing at GWDG, in an interview with Tom’s Hardware Premium. "This is the maximum speed. TOP500 does not tell us anything other than we have an instrument that could go that far."That speed matters because supercomputers are as much scientific instruments as anything else, used to simulate climate systems, aircraft engines, nuclear accidents and prospective fusion reactors. Scientists want answers relatively quickly. "Imagine I do the weather prediction for tomorrow, and you need 25 hours to calculate it," says Kunkel. By the time the answer arrives, so has tomorrow, rendering it useless.A mixed pictureThe HPCG test and its sparse calculations make less efficient use of processors while putting greater strain on memory bandwidth, latency, and communication between nodes – the sorts of things that scientific applications really need. LineShine's first-place score of 22 petaflops on this measure suggests that its memory and interconnect systems are as powerful as its CPUs. "Those results describe different capabilities, not a contradiction," said Dongarra, responding to Tom’s Hardware Premium’s questions by email.But another ranking looks at performance in a different way. The way HPL-MxP is designed favors GPUs and dedicated tensor or matrix engines. On this one, LineShine nabbed fourth place globally with 7.92 exaflops, a 3.6-fold increase over its HPL result. But the published HPL and HPL-MxP lists show the accelerator-heavy El Capitan achieved a 9.2-fold improvement, Aurora 11.5-fold and Frontier 8.4-fold.Dongarra said the different results on different checks show a trade-off in specialization, rather than a universal weakness. LineShine's CPU-centered design has less dedicated low-precision throughput, so other machines do better on mixed-precision workloads – but he said it would be churlish to say LineShine is less capable overall. And the IO500 – which Kunkel co-founded — tests storage bandwidth and metadata performance, while Green500 divides HPL performance by power consumption. What to read next Chinese Z.ai's latest model tops AI ranking charts amid Anthropic Fable 5 ban Kimi K3 rocks the AI industry as Moonshot AI undercuts closed-source American competitors on price China's homegrown AI accelerators to supply 90% of the country's domestic market, analysts suggest The different metrics by which supercomputers can be measured mean that those procuring them often overlook the rankings in favor of things like time-to-solution and reliability or energy use.What about AI?The race for public supercomputing has been disrupted by the rise of private AI infrastructure. Although Microsoft's Eagle system appears at number seven in the latest TOP500, most frontier AI clusters publish only GPU counts, theoretical FP8 performance, or tokens-per-second claims – and some don’t really disclose much at all publicly, worried that their competitors might pick up on it.There are some AI-based testing regimes out there, including MLPerf, which offers standardized AI training and inference tests, including new DeepSeek-V3 and GPT-OSS 20B workloads in its 2026 training suite. However, submissions to the scoring system remain voluntary, and AI labs might not want to submit them in case they score badly, torpedoing their public perception — meaning we know very little about some of the world's most consequential computing systems.It’s also a distraction, said the experts. "There is no sense for any private AI system to run HPL," said Kunkel. Doing so would take thousands of expensive accelerators away from commercial work and require days of tuning a result their customers don’t use, and probably don’t care about.Dongarra reckons LineShine probably isn’t best at everything, even though among those systems that are submitting public results, it showed the strongest measured double-precision and HPCG performance. That, he believes, makes it good enough to say this is a very good supercomputer. Any credible assessment, he said, "requires a portfolio of measurements" — covering time-to-solution, sustained performance under mixed workloads, reliability, ease of programming, cost and power alongside the headline benchmarks.So while LineShine's HPL victory is significant and technically impressive, it also highlights how there is no longer one supercomputer race. Systems whose results are never disclosed may be faster for particular AI workloads, "but without comparable public evidence,” said Dongarra, “that remains a claim rather than a ranking".
items.author: Chris Stokel-Walker
items.titleZh: The supercomputer race no longer means what it used to, as rankings lose relevance in the AI era — as privately held compute clusters are built, running HPL becomes a distraction
items.descriptionZh:
2026年6月TOP500榜单中，中国超级计算机LineShine强势登顶，凭借近2.2 exaflops（每秒22亿亿次双精度浮点运算）的性能，成为全球最快的公开展示超算系统。这台位于深圳国家超算中心的机器，一举终结了美国El Capitan的榜首地位，也在注重实际应用性能的HPCG竞赛中夺得第一。然而，所谓“世界最快”的结论并不统一：在面向混合精度的HPL-MxP测试中，LineShine仅列第四；在能效比排名的Green500榜单上更是远远落后。这种不同榜单上的位次差异，折射出超级计算机竞赛已经不再是单一维度的速度比拼，而是多套标准、多种测度、多个游戏规则并存的复杂局面。

LineShine的核心技术全部来自中国本土生态。它基于凌鲲平台，采用专有的凌琦互连和麒麟操作系统，内部集成了多达1379万个处理器核心，核心来自304核的LX2处理器。这是TOP500历史上首台纯CPU机器持续突破2 exaflops大关，实测性能达到理论峰值的约80%，而整机功耗高达42.2兆瓦。如此亮眼的数字，使LineShine成为自2017年以来第一台登顶TOP500的中国系统。此前中国已停止将最先进机器提交公开排名，TOP500联合创始人Jack Dongarra曾推测，可能已有两套未公开的中国系统，其性能超过当时美国领先的Frontier。

TOP500自1993年起采用高性能Linpack基准（HPL）作为排序依据。该基准要求机器用双精度算术求解一个稠密线性方程组，这种高度规则的计算可通过大量调优来压榨硬件潜力，非常适合跨架构、跨年代的长期对比。但正如哥廷根大学高性能计算教授Julian Kunkel所言，HPL只展示了一台机器的极限速度，好比告诉你一辆保时捷能开到400公里每小时，但现实中的科学负载往往不是这种跑法。超级计算机是用于模拟气候系统、飞机发动机、核事故、聚变反应堆等复杂问题的科学仪器，用户真正关心的是在合理时间内获得答案——如果明天要用的天气预报需要25小时才能算完，那结果出来时已经毫无意义。

为了弥补HPL的局限，HPCG基准采用稀疏计算，让处理器利用效率下降，同时重点考验内存带宽、延迟和节点间通信——这些才是真实科学应用最需要的瓶颈环节。LineShine在此项得到22 petaflops，排名第一，证明其内存层次和互连系统与强大的CPU相得益彰。Dongarra向Tom's Hardware Premium表示，不同测试描述的是不同能力，并不构成矛盾。在混合精度的HPL-MxP测试中，LineShine实现7.92 exaflops，是自身HPL成绩的3.6倍，但同样使用加速卡的对手提升更大：El Capitan为9.2倍，Aurora为11.5倍，Frontier为8.4倍。这说明LineShine面向低精度矩阵运算的专用硬件比例相对较少，属于专业化取舍，而非全面落后。此外，还有专门衡量存储带宽和元数据性能的IO500，以及按功耗折算性能的Green500。采购方往往更关心求解时间、可靠性、能耗等实际指标，而不会紧盯单一榜首。

近年来，私有AI基础设施的崛起也在重塑超级计算机的叙事。虽然微软的Eagle系统出现在最新TOP500第七位，但大多数前沿AI集群只公布GPU数量、理论FP8算力或每秒处理token数，甚至干脆不公开任何可验证数据，生怕竞争对手获知内情。MLPerf等标准化AI训练和推理测试提供了参考，但提交纯属自愿，AI实验室若在公众面前表现不佳，反而会损害形象，因此很多最重要的计算系统处于黑箱状态。专家们认为，向私有AI系统强制跑HPL毫无意义：这需要将数千张昂贵的加速卡从商业任务中抽离，花数天时间调优用户根本不关心的成绩。Dongarra指出，即使LineShine并非在所有单项上都是最强，但在所有公开提交结果的系统中，它表现出最强的双精度和HPCG性能，已经足以称得上一台非常优秀的超级计算机。任何可信的评估都需要一组综合测量，涵盖求解时间、混合负载下的持续性能、可靠性、编程便利性、成本和功耗，而不只是几个头条基准。

LineShine问鼎HPL在技术上意义重大，但更重要的是，它再次表明“超级计算机竞赛”早已不复存在。那些从不公开结果的系统，也许在特定AI工作负载上更快，但在缺少可比性公开展示证据的情况下，这只是一种主观声称，而不是一个可验证的排名。超级计算机的优劣，从此只能是多维度数据拼图，而非一张简单的冠军榜。

items.title: SMIC posts record $3B quarter and hikes wafer prices — US sanctions hand Chinese foundry a captive AI market
items.description: SMIC posted its first $3 billion quarter earlier this month, with revenue up 36.1% year on year, net profit nearly tripling to $479.2 million.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter SMIC posted its first $3 billion quarter earlier this month, with revenue up 36.1% year on year, net profit nearly tripling to $479.2 million. Co-CEO Zhao Haijun told analysts the next day that the Shanghai foundry will charge more for wafers processed in the third quarter after price negotiations concluded in the first. Utilization hit 93.7% against demand Zhao said SMIC can't fully meet, driven by Chinese AI data center buildouts that U.S. export controls have cut off from TSMC and Samsung at the leading edge. "Since there's still a big gap between industry-leading wafer prices and SMIC's current prices, we need to negotiate with customers for fairer pricing," Zhao said on the call.The quarter blew SMIC's own out of the water on every front. The company had guided to 14% to 16% sequential revenue growth and a 20% to 22% gross margin; it delivered 20% growth to $3.01 billion and a 25.3% margin, up from 20.1% in Q1. Wafer shipments rose 14% quarter-on-quarter to 2.9 million 8-inch equivalents, blended selling prices climbed 5.7%, and Q3 guidance calls for a 26% to 28% gross margin. China accounted for 90% of revenue.Demand isn’t coming from GPUs, however, with Zhao commenting that the surge came mostly from AI chips other than CPUs and GPUs, such as logic ICs, BCD power-management parts, and optical transceiver components, all in short supply. Meanwhile, growth in SMIC’s AI peripheral segment is expected to be around 40% for the quarter, while industrial and automotive chips rose to 16.5% of wafer revenue from 10.6% a year earlier.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: From bust to boomSMIC's utilization sat at 68.1% in the first quarter of 2023 and averaged 75% that year as net profit fell more than 60% and gross margin dropped 16.4 points to 21.9%. As late as early 2025, it was reported that SMIC and Hua Hong were cutting mature-node prices to defend share against a wall of new Chinese capacity. The company that spent 2023 and 2024 discounting into overcapacity spent 2026 raising prices by around 10% in December, negotiating targeted increases in capacity-constrained segments in February, and applying another round to Q3 wafers.Export controls did most of the work, with Washington’s restrictions keeping China's AI accelerator demand away from TSMC. Beijing has been redirecting that demand inward: the government wants 70% of silicon wafers sourced domestically this year, and a Bloomberg Intelligence survey of 60 Chinese tech executives in June found firms plan to spend 46% of their AI accelerator budgets on local chips over the next 12 months, up from 30% now. SMIC is the only Chinese foundry that mass-produces 7nm-class logic, which makes it the sole domestic route to silicon for Huawei's Ascend line and Cambricon's accelerators. A protected buyer pool, along with a mandated shift to domestic supply and a single qualified supplier at the leading edge, produces a textbook seller's market. You may like Trailing-edge foundry roadmaps for GlobalFoundries, UMC, and SMIC Samsung raises advanced foundry prices by up to 15% as AI demand fills its 4nm lines, report claims China claims chip exports nearly doubled to $177 billion in the first half of 2026 as memory prices surged Hua Hong, China's second-largest foundry, reported utilization of 102.8% in the same week, with record revenue of $717.5 million, up 26.8% year on year. TrendForce data shows foundry prices across China rose 5% to 15% between Q1 and Q2, with a third round of increases being prepared for the second half. TSMC is reportedly raising prices across all its advanced nodes too, so SMIC's hikes track a global trend, but SMIC is doing it from a captive position TSMC doesn't have: its customers have no other choice.China's AI chip designers post record first halves Cambricon's first-half revenue rose 108% to 6 billion yuan (c. $890 million) with net profit up 122.6% to 2.3 billion yuan, per its Shanghai Stock Exchange filing reported by the South China Morning Post. Moore Threads grew first-half revenue 147% to 1.74 billion yuan and cut its net loss by 96%, and Biren projected first-half revenue growth of more than 1,850% off a small base ahead of a Hong Kong IPO. Memory maker CXMT raised $8.6 billion in Shanghai's biggest-ever semiconductor listing last month and surged 466% on debut to become the most valuable company on any mainland exchange. Every one of these firms sits on the U.S. Entity List or depends on suppliers that do, and every one just posted record or near-record numbers.Beijing had until recently been blocking Chinese imports of U.S. accelerators. The US approved around 10 Chinese firms to buy Nvidia's H200 in May, but China had been blocking the purchases to protect domestic suppliers. Under Secretary of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler told a congressional hearing on July 14 that "very few" H200s had actually shipped. Officials have relented as of August 19, with ByteDance and Tencent each having received around 10,000 H200 chips, the first meaningful deliveries since the U.S. approved around 10 Chinese firms as buyers.Some 20,000 delivered accelerators against Huawei's target of 600,000 Ascend 910Cs this year leaves Chinese cloud spending, which Goldman Sachs pegs at roughly $102 billion for 2026 in combined AI capex across Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, and Baidu, landing overwhelmingly on domestic silicon.SMIC's 7nm yields and the HBM shortage SMIC's leading-edge economics remain brutal, however, with industry sources cited by the Financial Times putting SMIC's 5nm and 7nm prices 40% to 50% above TSMC's with yields of less than a third, a consequence of running multi-patterned DUV on nodes designed for EUV. The wafers SMIC is repricing are overwhelmingly mature-node parts, where its cost position is sound; the advanced capacity that feeds Ascend production stays yield-limited and expensive per good die regardless.Memory, not logic, caps accelerator output anyway, and SemiAnalysis estimates Huawei has been drawing down a stockpile of roughly 13 million Samsung HBM stacks acquired before the late-2024 controls, and domestic HBM from CXMT will cover only a fraction of 2026 Ascend targets.SMIC's own profit surge also comes with a glaring asterisk: CFO Wu Junfeng said the near-tripling was boosted by a one-time gain from a subsidiary. Demand for its silicon rests largely on policy rather than proven end markets, with an analyst tally cited by Asia Times putting China's top 11 listed chip firms at a combined average of roughly 122 times projected 2026 earnings.

items.titleZh: SMIC posts record $3B quarter and hikes wafer prices — US sanctions hand Chinese foundry a captive AI market
items.descriptionZh:
中芯国际最近公布了首份单季营收突破30亿美元的财报：营收同比增长36.1%至30.1亿美元，净利润4.792亿美元，几乎是去年同期三倍。公司联席CEO赵海军在财报电话会上表示，由于第一季度已完成价格谈判，第三季度晶圆代工价格将上调；目前产能利用率达93.7%，但仍无法满足需求。这份成绩全面超越公司自身指引——此前预期营收环比增长14%-16%、毛利率20%-22%，实际环比增长20%、毛利率25.3%（Q1为20.1%）。晶圆出货量环比增长14%至290万片等效8英寸，混合均价上涨5.7%，Q3毛利率指引为26%-28%。中国大陆收入占比达90%。

赵海军称，本轮需求并非来自GPU，而主要来自除CPU/GPU以外的AI芯片，比如逻辑IC、BCD电源管理芯片和光收发器组件，这些器件均供不应求。公司AI配套业务当季预计增长约40%；工业和汽车芯片占晶圆收入比重从一年前的10.6%升至16.5%。

这一猛涨背后是美国出口管制。华盛顿的禁令使中国AI加速器需求无法流向台积电和三星先进工艺，北京则大力推动国产化：政府要求今年70%的硅片本土采购；彭博行业研究调查60位中国科技高管显示，未来12个月企业计划将46%的AI加速器预算用于本土芯片，目前为30%。中芯国际是唯一量产7nm级逻辑芯片的国内代工厂，因此华为昇腾、寒武纪加速器只能依赖它。受保护买家池、强制国产化、先进节点唯一供应商，构成教科书式卖方市场。

这也是从衰退到景气的逆转。2023年Q1中芯国际利用率仅68.1%，全年平均75%，净利跌超60%，毛利率下滑16.4个百分点至21.9%；2023-2024年公司为应对产能过剩而降价，如今则持续提价：2025年12月已上调约10%，2026年2月针对受限产能谈判定向涨价，并计划对Q3晶圆再涨一轮。TrendForce数据显示，中国代工价格Q1-Q2上涨5%-15%，下半年正酝酿第三轮涨价。台积电也在对所有先进制程提价，但中芯国际拥有台积电没有的“锁定客户”：客户别无选择。

产业链上下游同样受益。华虹半导体同期产能利用率达102.8%，营收7.175亿美元创纪录，同比增26.8%。寒武纪上半年营收60亿元（约合8.9亿美元），同比增108%，净利23亿元增122.6%；摩尔线程上半年营收17.4亿元，增147%，净亏损收窄96%；壁仞科技赴港IPO前预计上半年营收增长超1850%（基数低）；长鑫存储上个月在上海完成规模最大的半导体IPO，融资86亿美元，首日涨466%，成为内地交易所市值最高的公司。这些企业均被列入美国实体清单或依赖清单上的供应商，但都交出创纪录业绩。

美国对华AI芯片出口近期松动。今年5月美方批准约10家中国企业购买英伟达H200，但中方为保护本土供应商曾阻止采购；美商务部副部长杰弗里·凯斯勒7月14日透露“极少数”H200已实际出货。直到8月19日，字节跳动和腾讯各收到约1万片H200，这是获批后首批实质交付。约2万片进口加速器对比华为今年60万片昇腾910C的生产目标微不足道。高盛预计2026年阿里、腾讯、字节、百度合计AI资本开支约1020亿美元，其中绝大多数将投向国产芯片。

然而中芯国际先进制程的经济性依然残酷。金融时报援引行业消息称，其5nm和7nm价格比台积电高40%-50%，良率不到台积电三分之一，原因是用多重曝光深紫外（DUV）光刻制造原本为极紫外（EUV）设计的器件。不过本轮涨价晶圆主要是成熟节点，成本结构健康；而为昇腾提供的先进产能仍受限于良率，每颗合格芯片成本高昂。此外，真正限制加速器产量的是存储而非逻辑。SemiAnalysis估计，华为在2024年底管制前囤积了约1300万片三星HBM（高带宽内存），而长鑫国产HBM只能覆盖2026年昇腾目标的一小部分。

最后还需注意，中芯国际近三倍的净利润增长包含一次性收益——CFO吴俊峰承认其中来自子公司的一次性收益。需求也更多建立在政策而非成熟市场上；据亚洲时报引述分析师统计，中国11家主要上市芯片公司基于2026年预期利润的平均市盈率约122倍，估值风险不容忽视。

history.title: Dell XPS 13 (2026) review: the new bar for mainstream Windows laptop excellence
history.description: The return of the XPS 13 is a triumph of (somewhat) affordable premium portable computing. It’s no powerhouse in terms of performance, but it gets more than enough right to recommend for Windows users who have been looking over their shoulder at the MacBook Neo.
history.content: A year after killing off its long-running XPS premium consumer brand, Dell did an about-face at CES early this year, promising new models, including the redesigned XPS 13 we’re looking at here. But between Dell’s announcement and the XPS 13’s launch, Apple stunned the portable PC world with its budget-priced, unquestionably pretty MacBook Neo, at a starting price of $599 (which got bumped up to $699 in June), leaving even Windows die-hards wondering how PC makers were going to compete in the budget and mid-range laptop space.Dell clearly decided the XPS 13 was its answer to the Neo, giving it a starting price of $699 for the model with 8GB of RAM (comparable to the Neo), or $899 for the 16GB model. Both options sport the same 512GB of SSD storage and an Intel Series 3 Core 5 320 (Wildcat Lake) CPU. We tested both the 8GB and 16GB models, though there is little difference outside of memory capacity.Design of the Dell XPS 13 (2026) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)The XPS 13 may lack the design flourishes of previous XPS models (there is no carbon fiber to be found), but if I had to describe the new XPS 13’s look in one word, it would be “refined.” Available in the silver “sky” color of our review unit, or a darker gray “storm” hue, all the edges are rounded, and the all-aluminum chassis feels premium, with only some slight flex. And I like the understated branding, with a slim, mirrored XPS logo on top and a smaller mirrored Dell logo underneath.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Dell XPS 13 DX13260 (2026) at Dell for $699.99It’s a look that generally doesn’t stray far from the Apple laptop standard, but the XPS 13 actually feels better in the hands than the MacBook Neo. At 11.69 x 7.9 x 0.5 inches, the Dell’s dimensions roughly match the Neo (11.71 x 8.12 x 0.5 inches), but the XPS is a half-pound lighter (2.2 pounds for the Dell versus 2.7 pounds for the Apple), and Dell tapers its edges more, making it feel slimmer. Both are attractive laptops, to be sure, but having held them both side-by-side, I slightly prefer the XPS 13. And considering how much the MacBook Neo wowed the consumer tech world earlier this year, that’s an impressive achievement from Dell. Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original Port selection is relegated to a single USB-C port on either side. But with the XPS 13, both are 10 Gbps ports that support DisplayPort 2.1 and charging, while Apple’s competition has one 10 Gbps port and one much slower USB 2.0 port (both are USB-C). Apple does include a headphone jack, which the XPS 13 lacks, and that will be annoying for some. But Dell includes a keyboard backlight while Apple leaves your fingers to fumble around in the dark. Personally, I’d take a backlight over an audio jack any day.The only thing I don’t love about the new XPS 13’s design is the somewhat sharp edge of metal at the bottom rear, behind the exhaust vents. Because the laptop is so slim and light, I found myself grabbing it by any and all angles, and this is the one area where it doesn’t feel premium or comfortable to hold.Dell XPS 13 (2026) Specifications Swipe to scroll horizontally CPU Intel Series 3 Core 5 320 Graphics Intel Graphics (2 Xe cores) Memory 8GB or 16GB (single-channel LPDDR5 at 7467 MT/s) Storage 512GB SSD Display 13.4-inch, 2560 x 1600, touch Networking Intel Wi-Fi 7 BE213 2x2, Bluetooth 6.0 Ports 2x USB 3.2 Gen 2 (10 Gbps) Camera 1080p, IR Battery 52 Whr Power Adapter 65W USB-C Operating System Windows 11 Home Dimensions (WxDxH) 11.69 x 7.9 x 0.5 inches Weight 2.2 pounds (1 kg) Price (as configured) $699 (8GB), $899 (16GB) Today's best Dell XPS 13 DX13260 (2026) deals $699.99View No price informationCheck Amazon No price informationCheck Best BuyWe check over 250 million products every day for the best pricesProductivity Performance on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)We tested both the 8GB and 16GB variants of the XPS 13. Aside from RAM capacity, the two machines share the same Intel “Wildcat Lake” Series 3 Core 5 320 CPU, with two Performance cores that can Turbo up to 4.6 GHz and four Efficient cores that can hit 3.4 GHz.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsBoth systems also make do with 512GB of SSD storage (there are no other capacity options). As we’ll get into in our testing, while the performance is roughly similar, our XPS systems had two different drives: one from SK hynix and the other from Kioxia.As for comparisons, we’ve included the similarly priced (at least to the 8GB mode) MacBook Neo. And on the Windows side, we’ve included the Chuwi UniBook, which has a plastic chassis and a lesser Wildcat Lake CPU, as well as Dell’s XPS 14 with a more powerful Core Ultra 7 355 CPU and a much higher price of nearly $2,000 as tested. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)On Geekbench 6, the XPS 13 bested the Chuwi UniBook with its lesser Core 3 304 CPU, but fell behind the MacBook Neo, and by no small amount on the single-core test. The pricier, Panther Lake-powered XPS 14, interestingly, fell right in line with XPS 13 on this test. But as we’ll see next, that doesn’t mean the two systems perform the same on all tasks. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)With eight cores and a higher power envelope to work with, the XPS 14 easily led here, converting our 4K test file to 1080p in under seven minutes. This points out the benefits of a higher-powered system for doing compute-intensive tasks like video editing. The XPS 13, particularly the 8GB model, was a bit behind the MacBook Neo, while the Chuwi laptop lagged more than a minute behind everything else. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Both versions of the Dell XPS 13 looked good in our 25GB file transfer test, but the 16GB model was significantly faster. Dell, like most laptop makers, doesn’t guarantee drive models in specific laptops. But in our two units, the 16GB model had an SK hynix PVC10 SSD, while the 8GB model sported a Kioxia BG7 (both drives are 512GB).The SK hynix drive was about 350 MB/s faster here, but the MacBook Neo was about half as fast as even the slower XPS 13, and the Chuwi UniBook was half as fast again, not a whole lot faster than a spinning-platter hard drive.If you’re wondering about gaming on the XPS 13, you probably shouldn’t, unless you’re a fan of retro titles and 2D side-scrollers. The CPU’s integrated graphics make do with just two Intel Xe cores. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)In 3DMark’s Steel Nomad, neither the 8GB XPS 13 nor the Chuwi UniBook (which also has 8GB of RAM) would run the test. The MacBook Neo (369) easily edged past the 16GB XPS 13 (369). But the Panther Lake-powered Dell XPS 14 (with twice as many Xe cores) more than doubled the results of its smaller sibling.To stress test the CPU in laptops, we run 10 loops of Cinebench 2026. The 16GB version of the system started with a score of 1,443, dipped to 1,374, but then ramped up (presumably as the cooking kicked in) to 1701, and then finished the rest of its runs steadily in the high 1600s. During the test, the laptop’s Core 5 320 CPU’s six cores averaged a clock speed of 3.13 GHz. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Interestingly, the 8GB model of the XPS 13 (which again has the same CPU) scored slightly lower than the 16GB version on all but the second run. And that’s likely down solely to the memory limitation. As the benchmark’s developer Maxson explains, running Cinebench 2026 on a system with less than 8.5 GB of RAM “will utilize virtual memory, which triggers a significant amount of paging, lowering the achievable performance.”There’s little doubt that demanding real-world applications will cause similar performance dips. So even if you think you’re good about closing tabs or don’t otherwise do a lot of multitasking, you may get better performance out of the 16GB model. And if you regularly do demanding tasks like editing video or any kind of rendering, you should opt for something more powerful. Wildcat Lake laptops and the MacBook Neo are designed for lightweight tasks like Web browsing and basic document creation.8GB vs 16GBOutside of benchmarks, the biggest question between the 8GB and 16GB configurations is: What is it actually like to use Windows 11 on these systems?The short answer, unsurprisingly, is that 16GB is better. With 15 identical tabs open in Chrome, the 16GB system just ran smoother. You might have to look closely at the Windows animations to notice, but they were far more fluid with more memory. And more importantly, switching back and forth between tabs was faster on the 16GB version, with the 8GB systems’ browser often blinking white before showing a page again.Chrome (as well as multiple other browsers) does offer a feature to put tabs to sleep while you're not using them. If you're a multitasker in the browser, you'll absolutely want to make sure this is turned on.For even the most basic tasks, it would behoove Microsoft to make Windows as efficient as possible, because it shouldn't take just a few tabs to start making the experience worse.Displays on the Dell XPS 13 (2026) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Dell doesn’t specify the panel type it uses for the XPS 13, but the 2560 x 1600 touch display generally looks good. And its 30-120 Hz refresh is a nice touch that should help battery life in some scenarios. We did, though, notice an issue with our 16GB review unit. When playing back video, the screen often flickered during bright scenes – but only when running on battery. It went away once the laptop was plugged in, which led me to dig into the display settings, where I noticed the dynamic refresh rate was set to be turned off when on battery. Enabling variable refresh made the flickering go away. Dell told us dynamic research should be told on by default.There is a separate display wrinkle, though. When placing the 8GB and 16GB models side-by-side, there were some clear differences between the two panels. The 8GB’s screen had deeper blacks, but noticeable backlight glow along the edges of the black bars while watching movie trailers. The 16GB model, however, had worse viewing angles. So both screens had their own upsides and drawbacks. Interestingly, as we’ll see below, the two panels' measurements are quite similar, but one is made by Sharp, while the other is from LG.Like the SSDs, Dell told us that it is multi-sourcing panels. "You’ve seen some variances with individual panels, but each panel should meet the specs set out for XPS 13," a Dell representative told Tom's Hardware. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)In our testing, the XPS 13’s screen delivered over 100% of the sRGB gamut, and roughly 75% of the larger DCI-P3 space.The MacBook Neo’s screen was similarly colorful, but at a measured 452.6 nits, it’s a little brighter than the XPS 13’s panel, which topped out just below 400 nits. But the XPS panels also include touch, which all MacBooks still lack (at least for now). Both the Dell and the Apple systems deliver great screens for machines in this price range. The Chuwi, while a cheaper laptop, also delivers a screen that’s much less colorful and dimmer than the competition.Keyboard and touchpad on the Dell XPS 13 (2026) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)I wouldn’t call the XPS 13’s chiclet-style keyboard one of its strong suits – key travel is fairly shallow, and the keys feel a little stiff. But the slight travel isn’t surprising in a laptop that’s half an inch thick, and I feel like I would get used to the slight stiffness fairly quickly. I didn’t notice any layout issues that confused my fingers, and I could see myself happily using this keyboard for hours a day without any real complaints.The chiclet style differs from what Dell offers on the XPS 14 and XPS 16, which has the keys placed next to each other in a "lattice-free" design. While I wish there was a bit more travel on the XPS 13, I personally prefer the more traditional chiclet keys over what the company is doing with its larger XPS options.The touchpad is fairly roomy for a laptop this small, at over five inches. And it’s a physical click pad rather than haptic, but it doesn’t feel cheap. It performed well during my testing time, and is otherwise unremarkable. I like that its top is set just slightly recessed below the deck so both my eyes and my fingers always know where it starts and ends, unlike the previous version of the XPS 13, where its haptic pad was built seamlessly into the wrist area.That said, the XPS 13’s trackpad, as is traditionally the case, only clicks when you press on or near the bottom. The Neo’s trackpad is also mechanical, but lets you click wherever your fingers land. I don’t particularly find the Neo’s trackpad feature a substantial advantage, but if you’re used to a haptic touchpad, being able to click anywhere on the pad might feel more familiar.Audio on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)One thing I wasn’t expecting from the XPS 13 was great-sounding speakers. But for a system this slim and a price below $1,000, the quad-speaker setup here left my ears pleasantly surprised. I listened to Portion Control’s “Brain Scraper Death Dive (Rebuild),” and the 8W of peak output filled my home office with a surprising level of sound, without noticeable distortion, even at 100% volume. There’s even some noticeable bass – within reason, mind you. This is a half-inch thick, 2.2-pound laptop. But considering the XPS 13’s svelte frame and its starting price, the speakers and tuning are excellent.Upgradability of the Dell XPS 13 (2026)There are only four tiny Torx screws to remove on the bottom of the XPS 13. But after doing that, getting into the laptop was still quite difficult. Dell recommends prying with your thumbs from the rear center. That didn’t work for me no matter how hard I pushed. Eventually, with the help of a plastic pick-style pry tool, I was able to release a few clips near the slim side vents, then work my way around the edges. The clips where Dell recommends starting from near the rear center were the last to release, and some of the most tenacious I have dealt with in several years. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Once finally inside, there isn’t much to do except stare into the abyss of the stealth-black interior. Swapping the short 2230 M.2 SSD in the upper-right corner should be pretty easy. And replacing the battery down the road doesn’t look too difficult. But that’s all you’re likely to change in here.Perhaps most interesting for such a small laptop, Dell has equipped the XPS 13 with a pair of fans. Fan noise was audible as a whir, but I really only noticed it during our lengthy Cinebench 2026 stress test. And honestly, if you’re running tasks that tax the CPU for several minutes at a time like this, you should probably opt for something more powerful anyway.Battery life on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)The XPS 13 did well compared to similar options in our battery test, which consists of web browsing, running OpenGL tests, and streaming videos with the screen at 150 nits while connected to Wi-Fi. Both the 8GB and 16GB models of the XPS 13 easily topped 14 hours, which is roughly an hour to 90 mins more than the MacBook Neo and slightly better than the Chuwi. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Of particular interest is the half-hour shorter time on the 8GB model. Some of that difference could easily be down to testing variance. But the 8GB version we tested has a Kioxia BG7 SSD, while the 16GB version has an SK Hynix PVC10. Both are DRAMless drives, but the Hynix drive may be more power-efficient during our battery benchmark.At well over 20 hours, though, it’s the XPS 14 that walks away with the competition here, helped by the fact that its screen is a lower resolution (1,920 x 1,200) than most of the competition here. Still, an extra five-plus hours of unplugged productivity is another reason why you might want to pay more for the slightly larger-screened Dell.A laptop charger worth calling outWe don’t typically write much about chargers in laptop reviews, but the one that Dell includes with the XPS 13 is exactly the type that I’ve been asking laptop makers to shift to for years now. It’s a tiny charger with folding prongs that’s more typical of the type you might use with a smartphone, and it has a removable cable. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Given that some of the best chargers we’ve tested can charge laptops and are much smaller than a typical laptop brick, it’s nice to finally see a company ship a compact charger with a laptop that is on par in terms of portability with something you can buy yourself for about $25 or less. It would be even nicer if Dell had included a second USB-C port on the power brick so you could charge both your laptop and smartphone at the same time, but I guess I shouldn’t expect miracles. Still, I applaud Dell for including a compact charger with the XPS 13 and hope to see similar chargers from competing PC makers soon.Heat on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)During our 10-loop Cinebench 2026 stress test, the XPS 13’s keyboard got warm up near the top row, where we measured the temperature at 104 degrees Fahrenheit, but that was above 4 key, not where fingers typically rest. The touchpad (87 F) and keyboard deck (88.5 F) remained cooler, though. The bottom of the laptop topped out at 108.5 F, toward the back where the CPU lives. Internally, the Core 5 320’s cores averaged a toasty 87.49 degrees Celsius, with the pair of P cores occasionally spiking to 100 C (TJMax), indicating there is some thermal throttling.The high temps here perhaps explain in part why Dell opted to use two fans in the XPS 13. And while there is some light fan noise when the laptop is under heavy CPU stress, the sound isn’t sharp or otherwise annoying – at least to my middle-aged ears.Webcam on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)The webcam on the XPS 13 is “only” 1080p, but it delivered enough detail, generally accurate colors, and handled bright light from windows and overhead fixtures pretty well. And unlike some of the XPS models from yesteryear, it also sits in the top center of the bezel, where it belongs.There is some graininess when viewing things at full screen, but it’s far from the worst I’ve seen. This camera is perfectly capable of handling typical online meetings or classes without making most people want to plug in one of the best webcams instead.Software on the Dell XPS 13 (2026)Considering its fairly affordable price, I was pleasantly surprised at how clean and pristine the Windows 11 Home OS is on the XPS 13. You get some of the typical Windows cruft, like a shortcut to WhatsApp and LinkedIn. And there are a few Dell apps, like Optimizer (which mostly links to Windows settings and other apps) and the self-explanatory SupportAssistant. But there really isn’t anything else here, other than a bookmark in the default Edge browser to go to McAfee's website. It’s refreshing to use a new laptop with a Windows install that reminds me of custom-built PCs.Dell XPS 13 (2026) ConfigurationsDell offers the XPS 13 in two pretty similar configurations. For $699, you get an Intel Series 3 Core 5 320 CPU with a 512GB SSD and 8GB of RAM. For $200 more ($899), you get the same laptop with 16GB of RAM. Somewhat annoyingly, the 16GB model is only offered in the silver “sky” colorway, while the 8GB model is available in both “sky” and a darker gray “storm.”Keeping the SKUs simple is doubtlessly one way that Dell is keeping costs down. And obviously the cost and availability of RAM and storage is tough this year. But it still would be nice to see at least a 1TB option for those who need more room for local files.Bottom Line (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)While it’s no performance powerhouse, and $200 extra for a doubling of the RAM to a more comfortable 16GB still feels like a lot even in these times of endless AI demand, Dell’s redesigned XPS 13 is an excellent budget or mid-range machine (depending on which model you choose). It’s light and slim enough that you’ll likely hardly notice it in a backpack, and with over 14 hours of battery life in our testing, it lasts longer than the MacBook Neo.Is it better than the MacBook Neo? In some ways, like the aforementioned battery life, keyboard backlighting, and weight, it is for sure. And for those worried about the limitations of 8GB, you can at least pay extra (again, that’s $200 extra) for 16GB with the XPS system. Really, though, the two devices are close enough in terms of performance, build quality, and portability that, if you are considering one or the other, you should probably choose the one with the operating system you prefer.The fact that Windows has a competitive machine to the disruptive MacBook Neo is a triumph for Dell, for Microsoft’s ecosystem, and for those of us (like me) who would just prefer not to get sucked into the Apple hardware orbit – not that Windows 11 doesn’t have a big basket full of flaws. Given how expensive everything else is these days (including most flagship premium laptops), it’s nice that Dell and Apple are delivering devices that look and feel good, without costing $1,000 or more. I wonder what the other PC makers will offer up to compete in this new $699-$899 premium laptop space.Dell XPS 13 DX13260 (2026): Price Comparison $699.99View No price informationCheck Amazon No price informationCheck Best BuyWe check over 250 million products every day for the best pricespowered by
